data.title: Mass-Mailing Self-Propagation
data.summary: The sample sends email from the infected host or a compromised mailbox to propagate itself or deliver further payloads, using the victim's own contacts or address book as a target list.
data.description:
Propagating through a victim's own contact list or compromised mailbox lends the outbound
message inherited trust — recipients see a message from someone they genuinely know,
which defeats the usual heuristic of distrusting unfamiliar senders. Implementations range
from driving a local mail client's send function directly, to authenticating against a
compromised webmail or SMTP account and sending independently of any client the victim
uses.
data.recommendation:
* Audit the compromised account's sent-mail folder and server-side logs for the full recipient list, since the victim's own client history may not show server-side sends.
* Rotate credentials for any mail account the sample had access to, and review for forwarding rules or app-password grants added alongside the compromise.
* Notify recipients promptly; a message from a genuinely known sender is more likely to be acted on, raising the urgency of containment relative to the initial infection alone.
data.short_recommendation: Audit server-side sent-mail logs for the full recipient list, and rotate credentials for the compromised account.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Authenticated against the victim's webmail account via stolen session cookies and sent a copy of itself to every contact in the address book.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Harvested the address book and sent itself to every contact using the compromised account's own send capability.
